title: ChiMED
slugLine: A wristband that reads the three pulse points of Traditional Chinese Medicine and uses AI to turn them into preventive health guidance.

figure.alt: Render of the ChiMED wristband: a white band with a grey display panel on top and a pad of three sensor rows on the inside.

research.problem: Healthcare is ==expensive== and the system cannot be changed, so **people would prefer to avoid hospitals altogether**.

stakeholders.name: Busy professionals
stakeholders.note: Mr. Zhang, 35, a product manager in Shanghai

stakeholders.name: People managing chronic conditions
stakeholders.note: Ms. Mei, 45, a grocery store owner with type 2 diabetes

stakeholders.name: Older adults without cover
stakeholders.note: Irving, 66, after his Medicare fell through

painPoints.label: Rising costs
painPoints.detail: Health expenditure per capita has risen 70% since 2015, and 27% of people avoid seeking care because it costs too much.

painPoints.label: Long waits for small check-ups
painPoints.detail: Big hospitals are expensive and time-consuming, and long waits for minor check-ups make regular physicals hard to fit in.

painPoints.label: Health apps people do not trust
painPoints.detail: Health apps are confusing or overly technical, their advice is vague, and users worry about data privacy and AI accuracy.

painPoints.label: No view between visits
painPoints.detail: TCM doctors have little time for deep pulse analysis on busy clinic days and find it hard to track patients between visits.

painPoints.label: Doubts about TCM
painPoints.detail: Patients who do not fully understand TCM hesitate, and doctors struggle to win the trust of those who doubt it.

rows.target: 5% of US consumer-grade wearable medical devices

rows.kpi: Net worth of $18M after Stage A, $118M after Stage B

insights.insight: Wearable health tech is growing fast
insights.evidence: The market for IoT wearable health tech is projected to grow at a 25.8% CAGR over the next five years.

insights.insight: AI is ready to do the reading
insights.evidence: AI models now score 99% on quantitative reasoning and coding (MATH-500), enough to back computational automation.

insights.insight: TCM pulse diagnosis can work with sensors
insights.evidence: New research at UChina and Penn State gives proof of concept for integrating TCM with modern sensors, and they launched the first TCM pulse-diagnosis AI model.

insights.insight: People already look past conventional care
insights.evidence: 37% of people seek alternative medicine in place of traditional care, and health influencers who push alternative medicine have large followings on social media.

roadmap.what: Train and validate on data: more than 90% diagnostic precision, alpha users report better health
Partner with TCM doctors and apothecaries
Sell in traditional hospitals and TCM clinics, online, and in dense areas
Expand globally and into other diagnostic and health needs, or exit

design.lead: A wristband with three sensors reads the three TCM pulse points around the clock. Its app turns the readings into AI-driven diagnostics and lifestyle suggestions, and a premium tier adds a personalized herbal prescription filled by a local herbalist.

blocks.title: What it offers
items: Copay-free diagnostics: AI-driven analysis that diagnoses health conditions
Preventive care: lifestyle suggestions that reduce the need for doctor’s visits
24/7 monitoring of organ health: three sensors detect the three TCM pulse points

items.title: Monitor
items.body: The wristband monitors health 24/7 through the three TCM pulse points.

items.title: Read
items.body: The phone app shows organ-by-organ readings and AI-enabled care suggestions based on pulse patterns.

items.title: Prescribe
items.body: Premium users receive a personalized prescription for herbal TCM supplements.

items.title: Fill
items.body: A local herbalist fills the prescription and answers questions about its effects.

results.lead: The pitch ends in a three-stage raise, from a $90K seed to a $3.3M international round, with ==an estimated $118M net worth== at the end of Stage B.

rings.name: TAM
rings.label: Global wearable medical devices market
rings.note: 2024 value. Projected to reach $324.73B by 2030, a 17.2% CAGR (2024–2032).

rings.name: SAM
rings.label: US wearable medical devices market
rings.note: About 14.6% of the global market in 2024. Projected to reach $46.89B by 2030, a 23.4% CAGR.

rings.name: SOM
rings.label: US consumer-grade wearable medical devices
rings.note: The consumer-grade segment is 77.5% of the US market. ChiMED targets a 5% share: about $103M in the first year and $1.82B by 2030 ($46.89B × 77.5% × 5%).

rows.label: Internal
cells: Strengths: cheaper, easily accessible, convenient, user friendly, personalized medicine
Weaknesses: seen as less trustworthy and reliable, liability issues, finite functional data, technical limitations, integration challenges

rows.label: External
cells: Opportunities: healthcare growing more expensive, distrust in the medical system, rising interest in Eastern medicine
Threats: data privacy and security, ethical concerns, comfort with a doctor’s opinion over AI, increasing job insecurity

blocks.title: Funding stages
blocks.note: Funds go to marketing, AI model R&D, product optimization and taxes.
